connection_condition: transactions_1k.CustomerID corresponds to customers.CustomerID
description: A transaction is part of a customer's purchase history; the transaction record cannot be interpreted without the customer it belongs to.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.GasStationID corresponds to gasstations.GasStationID
description: A transaction takes place at exactly one gas station and is meaningless without that station context.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.ProductID corresponds to products.ProductID
description: The product purchased is a component of the transaction event.

connection_condition: gasstations.ChainID groups the stations sharing that chain identifier
description: A chain is composed of its member stations; station-level records are the members through which a chain is observed.

connection_condition: yearmonth.CustomerID corresponds to customers.CustomerID
description: A monthly consumption value belongs to exactly one customer and cannot exist without that customer.

connection_condition: yearmonth.Date stamps each consumption value with its calendar month
description: A consumption value is stamped by exactly one year-month period; the period is part of the identity of the measurement.

connection_condition: customers.Segment assigns each customer to one of the categories SME, LAM, KAM
description: Customers classified as SME, LAM or KAM form subsets of the customer population; each category is a specific class of customer.

connection_condition: customers.Currency is the settlement currency of the customer
description: The settlement currency is a property carried by the customer profile and applies to all of that customer's consumption and transactions.

connection_condition: gasstations.Country records the country of the station
description: The country is an attribute of the station and scopes which stations count as, for example, Czech Republic stations.

connection_condition: gasstations.Segment records the station type
description: The station type is an attribute of the station; it shares the column name Segment with the customer classification but denotes a different concept.

connection_condition: products.Description labels the product
description: Each product carries exactly one human-readable description used when products are listed.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.Date stamps the transaction with its calendar day
description: The transaction date is the day-level time attribute of the event.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.Time stamps the transaction with its clock time
description: The transaction time is the time-of-day attribute of the event.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.Amount is the quantity of the transaction
description: The amount is an event-level measure attached to the transaction record.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.Price is the monetary value of the transaction
description: The price is an event-level monetary measure attached to the transaction record.

connection_condition: the year prefix of the period code selects the months to combine
description: Annual consumption is derived by combining the monthly consumption values that share a calendar year.

connection_condition: the year's consumption is expressed per month following the workload definition
description: Average monthly consumption is derived from the year's consumption figures rather than stored directly.

connection_condition: two consecutive years' annual consumption values for the same group
description: The growth rate is derived from the annual consumption of two consecutive years.

connection_condition: monthly values are combined per month within one year and customer group
description: The peak consumption month is derived from the month-level consumption values of a year.

connection_condition: customer-level consumption totals within a segment and year are compared
description: The least consuming customer is derived by comparing customers' consumption totals within a segment.

connection_condition: both express calendar time, but the month period uses a six-character year-month code while the transaction date uses a day-level ISO date
description: The two time dimensions are related but not interchangeable: they differ in granularity and in covered window, so a month of consumption cannot be directly compared with a transaction day without aligning granularity.

Both describe the magnitude of fuel purchased, but at different grains: the transaction amount is a single purchase event, whereas monthly consumption is an aggregated customer-month figure. They are not interchangeable.

connection_condition: currency is attached to the customer that owns the consumption records
description: Consumption values are only comparable within one currency, because the currency is a property of the customer rather than of the consumption record.
The two segment concepts share a column name but have disjoint value domains and different meanings: customer size categories versus station types.
